source.title: The Quest for Equational Axiomatizations of Parallel Composition: Status and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Does there exist one binary auxiliary operator that preserves bisimulation equivalence and whose addition to the recursion-free fragment of CCS is sufficient to obtain a finite equational axiomatization of the parallel composition operator? Equivalently, prove or refute the conjecture that no single binary operation can finitely axiomatize parallel composition up to bisimulation, so that two auxiliary operators such as left merge and communication merge are necessary.
accepted.context_brief: Auxiliary operators for CCS parallel composition

accepted.question_text: For process algebras whose language includes parallel composition with synchronization, such as ACP, find equational axiomatizations for bisimilarity that are omega-complete.
Prove that observation congruence is not finitely equationally axiomatizable over the fragment of CCS that excludes recursion, relabelling, and restriction.
accepted.context_brief: Observation congruence over a CCS fragment

accepted.question_text: Prove the stronger version of the non-finite-axiomatizability claim for observation congruence: for the recursion-, relabelling-, and restriction-free CCS language, the negative result should remain true after extending the language by any finite collection of GSOS operations.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Many open problems still remain, specifically in the search for omega-complete axiomatizations for rich process description languages, but the margins of this paper are too small to list them all.
Establish results of comparable elegance and strength in the setting of concurrency theory to the formal-language-theory results discussed for concatenation, shuffle, languages, and pomsets.
